newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina mulling $1.5-$2.0 bln bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Argentina mulling $1.5-$2.0 bln bond issue.

text.p: Argentina, seeking to take advantage of favorable market conditions, is considering issuing between $1.5 billion and $2.0 billion in bonds this year to finance 1997 spending needs, Finance Secretary Pablo Guidotti said Thursday.
"These funds would be put in an account made available only on Jan 1, 1997," Guidotti told reporters.
He added that authorities will issue $120 million in a lire-denominated bond this year. They will also issue a 500 million yen bond in the first quarter of 1997.
Argentina will also issue a bond of between $400 million and $500 million this year to finance public sector dismissals and job retraining under the so-called second reform of state.
"This issue could be made in the domestic market," Guidotti said.
Guidotti said there was a treasury deficit of "slightly more than" $500 million in October and that fiscal revenue in November and December is expected to be $3.8 billion each.
"This level of collection will be reached because the full impact of the measures in the last fiscal package will take effect," he added. This included increases in taxes on fuel.
Argentina had reached agreement with the International Monetary Fund to have a fiscal deficit of $6 billion in 1996 and $3 billion in 1997.
Asked if the 1996 goal will be met, Guidotti said, "The situation is tough. We are making cuts but in principle if the collection comes in as projected we will meet the goal."

As in other occasions, the government has decided to postpone until January 1997 spending planned for 1996 such as payment of public sector salaries, pensions, some transfers to the provinces and other commitments, he said.
He said the budget committee of the lower house of Congress introduced changes that would put the deficit at $3.4 billion next year, $400 million more than agreed with the IMF.
"This will oblige us to think up new measures to reach the goals set with the IMF," he said.
